#1512. Three outside contenders who could replace Michael Carrick as Man United's next manager

By Ben Sully | 10 Nov 2026 23:44, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 04:08

Manchester United are said to be on the brink of parting ways with head coach Michael Carrick, with the team languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 matches.

While a final decision is yet to be confirmed, rumours are already swirling about who the club could pick as Carrick's replacement should they decide to change head coach over the international break.

USA boss Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly towards the top of the club's managerial shortlist, with his current contract believed to contain a release clause.

Meanwhile, the Red Devils have also been linked with former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe, ex-Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann and the vastly experienced Antonio Conte, who previously managed Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League.

While the aforementioned quartet are believed to be among the main contenders, there may be alternative candidates who are at least on Man United's radar.

With that in mind, Sports Mole highlights three outside picks the Red Devils could consider if they decide to replace Carrick.

According to the latest odds, Kieran McKenna is among the potential contenders for the Man United job, although he is seen as an outsider compared to the likes of Pochettino, Howe, Nagelsmann and Conte.

There is a temptation to say that McKenna ‘knows the club’, but instead of using that tired old cliche, it is perhaps better to say he is someone who will be well-known by many figures at the club, and with that, there is less uncertainty about the way he works as a coach.

McKenna spent a couple of years working as the Under-18 coach at Man United before he was promoted to the role of assistant manager, where he worked with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Jose Mourinho, Ralf Rangnick and Carrick.

The 40-year-old ultimately decided to forge his own path as a manager when he took the top job at Ipswich Town in December 2021, going on to lead the club to back-to-back promotions before suffering Premier League relegation in the 2024-25 campaign.

Ipswich stuck with McKenna and were rewarded with another promotion-winning season, but he ultimately decided against overseeing the club’s latest Premier League campaign, instead opting to take a break from football management.

Considering it has been five months since he made that decision, it is unclear whether McKenna is now ready to jump back into the game, although the chance to manage a club of Man United’s stature would surely be a convincing factor.

There may be a tendency to think he would be a similar appointment to Solskjaer and Carrick due to his previous connections with the club, but he has already built a stronger CV than the aforementioned pair, and his willingness to use width as a means of attack would suit a philosophy that has previously been associated with Man United.

With Fabian Hurzeler and Marco Rose currently impressing at Brighton & Hove Albion and Bournemouth, Man United may want to look to Bundesliga’s exciting coaching talent for their next boss.

Stuttgart boss Sebastian Hoeness is seen as one of the league’s best coaches, even though his side has struggled for consistency this season.

Hoeness got his first taste as a Bundesliga head coach at Hoffenheim, where he oversaw 11th and ninth-place finishes before taking a year out of management.

In April 2023, the 44-year-old got the call from Stuttgart, who were languishing at the bottom of the table at the time of his appointment.

Hoeness lifted the club out of the automatic relegation spots before he guided them to victory in the relegation/promotion playoff against Hamburg.

Stuttgart’s transformation under Hoeness was there for all to see when the club achieved a runners-up finish in 2023-24, their best league finish in 17 years.

While there was a drop-off in the next Bundesliga campaign, any frustration from a ninth-place finish was made to feel insignificant by Stuttgart’s triumphant DFB-Pokal, which ended the club’s 28-year wait for glory in the domestic cup.

Champions League qualification followed in the 2025-26 campaign, an achievement that means Hoeness is yet to experience an unsuccessful season at Stuttgart, the sort of consistency that Man United could certainly benefit from.

Hoeness has shown a willingness throughout his coaching career to select a formation that best suits the player profiles in his squad, while still having a clear philosophy to certain aspects of the game, including the willingness for his teams to push full-backs and wing-backs high in a bid to get in good crossing positions.

Out of the three options, Marcelino is the biggest curveball on this list, although he has much more senior management experience than McKenna and Hoeness.

While he may be relatively unknown to an English audience, he has a strong reputation in Spain as a wily operator who tends to command the respect of his players.

Marcelino has managed some of Spain’s biggest clubs, including Sevilla, Valencia and Athletic Club.

The 61-year-old guided Valencia to their first Copa del Rey triumph in 11 years in the 2018-19 season, while he beat Real Madrid for the Spanish Super Cup during his time in charge of Athletic.

However, he perhaps spent his best years in charge of Villarreal, first for a spell from 2013 to 2016 before spending three more years in charge from 2023 to 2026.

In his first stint in charge, Marcelino guided the Yellow Submarine to promotion before achieving three consecutive top-three finishes in La Liga and a run to the Europa League semi-finals in 2015-16.

After returning to the club in November 2023, the experienced coach steered the club to an eighth-place finish, before leading them to Champions League qualification in back-to-back seasons.

In fact, he guided the club to third spot last season, their best top-flight placing since finishing runners-up in 2007-08, but it proved to be his final campaign in charge after failing to agree terms on a new contract.

Inigo Perez’s struggle to find consistency since taking over the reins at Villarreal has only added to the sense that the club may have made a mistake by allowing him to depart.

However, Villarreal’s potential error may be an opportunity for another club, and while it would be a left-field decision to choose him as Carrick’s replacement, he possesses over 800 games of senior managerial experience, has already coached clubs with demanding fanbases and would not be fazed by the Red Devils’ precarious position in the Premier League relegation zone.

His pragmatism has sometimes been used against him as a criticism, but it may be just what Man United need after shipping 19 goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Marcelino's keenness to play quickly through the lines and hit teams on the counter may also suit a team that is struggling for confidence in midfield and has players in advanced areas who can race in behind defences.

#1511. Armenia vs Cyprus - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 10 Nov 2026 23:58, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 00:04

Armenia welcome Cyprus to the Vazgen Sargsyan Republican Stadium on Thursday evening for their penultimate League C fixture in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, the Collectives played out a goalless draw with Montenegro at the Podgorica City Stadium, while the Blue and Whites claimed a narrow 2-1 victory over Latvia in Nicosia.

After just missing out on promotion to League B in the 2024-25 campaign, finishing second in their group but falling to a thumping 9-1 aggregate defeat against Georgia in the promotion playoff, Armenia will have mixed feelings about how they have started their latest Nations League endeavours.

Despite starting their campaign on the front foot with a 2-0 victory over Latvia in Yerevan, the Collectives have since suffered defeats to Montenegro and Cyprus, although a goalless draw against the former in early October has just about kept Thursday’s hosts in contention for promotion from League C.

With two group matches remaining, Eghishe Melikyan’s men sit third in their respective group, though currently loitering three points below Cyprus in the table, Armenia almost certainly need to claim victory this week if they want any chance of progressing through to a playoff tie.

To do so, the Collectives will certainly have to be better than their recent form suggests too, as despite never before losing a home match against Cyprus, Armenia have claimed victory over the Blue and Whites in just one of their prior eight meetings.

Following a bitterly disappointing World Cup qualifying campaign, winning just one of their six matches to finish fourth in European Group H and sit five points below Romania in the playoff places, Cyprus will be content with how they have bounced back in their latest Nations League efforts.

Although they failed to win either of their first two competition outings, losing to Montenegro in their opening fixture before playing out a stalemate with Latvia, the Blue and Whites have truly kick started their promotion bid by claiming back-to-back victories and as a result sit in a promising position with just a pair of group matches remaining.

Heading into Thursday’s contest, Apostolos Mantzios’s side sit second in their group with a comfortable cushion over third-placed Armenia, but with Montenegro only three points ahead at the summit, Cyprus still have the opportunity to secure automatic promotion rather than a playoff place, providing plenty of incentive to extend their winning streak through to the end of the campaign.

Having won three of their previous five encounters with Armenia, including a 2-0 victory when the nations met at the GSP Stadium earlier on in the campaign, the Blue and Whites will certainly be confident that they can close down on top spot this week too and craft another chance at winning their place in League B.

Armenia will be without Eduard Spertsyan for Thursday’s contest after the midfielder recently picked up an Achilles tendon injury, while backup goalkeeper Henri Avagyan has also been ruled out.

Sergey Muradyan, Julio Bueno and Sunderland’s Finn Geragusyan round off the hosts’ injury list, though the Collectives are also missing Erik Simonyan, Kamo Hovhannisyan and Vahan Bichakhchyan from the latest squad selection due to a lack of match fitness.

With Henrikh Mkhitaryan retiring from international football in 2022 and Spertsyan out injured, Melikyan’s biggest goal threat on Thursday could well be Tenerife forward Grant-Leon Ranos, who is likely to lead the line for Armenia.

Cyprus are missing both Giannis Satsias and Konstantinos Sotiriou as the pair continue their recovery from muscle issues, while Omonia forward Andronikos Kakoullis remains sidelined with an undisclosed problem.

The Blue and Whites’ only other injury woe is Pafos goalkeeper Charalampos Kyriakidis, who suffered an arm issue in June, though the visitors will also be without Kostas Pileas after the 27-year-old fullback received a red card in last month’s meeting with Armenia.

Having already netted two goals in the current Nations League campaign, Burnley forward Marcus Edwards is undoubtedly Mantzios’s dangerman and is almost certain to start in midfield just behind Ioannis Pittas on Thursday.

Beglaryan; Piloyan, Simonyan, Harutyunyan, Tiknizyan; Iwu, K.Hovhannisyan; Serobyan, Manvelyan, N.Hovhannisyan, Ranos

Fabiano; Konomis, Kyprianou, Panagiotou, Malekkidis; Artymatas, Kastanos; Edwards, Loizou, Georgiou; Pittas

With their form slipping in recent matches and a gap beginning to open up between themselves and the promotion places, it is imperative that Armenia claim all three points against Cyprus if they are to have even the slightest chance of competing in League B when the 2028-29 Nations League campaign gets underway.

However, with the Blue and Whites enjoying a promising run of form and also chasing down Montenegro in the race for automatic promotion, we believe Armenia’s hopes of progressing will run their course on Thursday as the visitors to take all three points in Yerevan.

#1510. Xabi Alonso must look at HIMSELF, not the officials, as another questionable line-up sees Chelsea fold at Sunderland - and Cole Palmer wastes his chance to respond to Thomas Tuchel snub, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 11:14 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 17:34 EST, 8 November 2026

When searching for why Chelsea were beaten by the side who were sitting bottom of the Premier League, the temptation from Xabi Alonso might be to describe this defeat as a tale of two penalties.

First, Chelsea were denied one when Cole Palmer was sandwiched by Luke O'Nien and Jules Ahoka as he entered the Sunderland area, with the officials concluding the contact occurred outside of the box.

Then, Sunderland were awarded one when Brian Brobbey was brought down by Levi Colwill. The striker had hold of the defender at the same time, and arguably clipped his own heel upon second viewing, but Enzo Le Fee gladly accepted the opportunity to score the game's only goal.

However, it would be wrong to blame this deserved defeat on those two decisions alone. Referee Jarred Gillett and VAR Nick Hopton were weak but not the reason that Chelsea lost.

This was actually a tale of two strikers. Sunderland had one in the brilliant bully that is Brobbey, whereas Chelsea had nobody after Alonso yet again decided against starting Danny Welbeck.

In the three Premier League games played since Joao Pedro's injury – against Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and now Sunderland – Alonso has gone with Morgan Rogers as a false nine once and Pedro Neto twice. Welbeck was on the bench in all of those matches.

Sunderland handed Chelsea a brutal reality check as they climbed off the foot of the table

The visitors fell victim to two questionable penalty calls at the Stadium of Light

We are not saying the 35-year-old is the answer to all of Alonso's problems, but he is an actual No9 who scored 13 times in the Premier League for Brighton last season.

Neto was hardly going to have a high success rate when wrestling with centre backs for the long balls which were coming from Colwill and Co. It is a question that needs asking, therefore, especially after another loss.

Why did Chelsea sign Welbeck if not to play when Joao Pedro is injured?

Welbeck came on in the 62nd minute here, but by then, a familiar feeling was washing over Chelsea.

They lost 2-1 here at the very end of last season. Malo Gusto scored an own goal, Wesley Fofana was red carded, and Chelsea, managed by Calum McFarlane in the interim, failed to qualify for any form of European football.

They smacked of an utterly unserious side then, and resembled it here, too.

Chelsea had a week to prepare for this Premier League clash while Sunderland were playing – and losing – to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League.

Regis Le Bris' side had not won in the league since August. Yet they were the sharper of the two teams here.

It hardly helped Alonso that Chelsea's attackers never appeared at it individually.

Cole Palmer had a stinker. This was supposed to be an opportunity to show why Thomas Tuchel made a mistake in not naming him in his latest England squad. If anything, he helped make sure those accusations cannot be levelled at Tuchel over this break.

Xabi Alonso tinkered with his line-up and it failed to pay off in a second defeat in three games

Cole Palmer had a stinker in a woeful response to Thomas Tuchel's England snub

Rogers' performance was best summed up by the time he simply sprinted out of play with the ball to gift Sunderland a goal-kick. He and Palmer resembled no-shows.

Sunderland (4-2-3-1): Roefs 6; Hume 7, Mukiele 7, O'Nien 6, Mandava 7; Xhaka 6 (Ahoka 4, 6), Sadiki 7; Meunier 6, Talbi 6 (Rigg 88), Le Fee 6 (Angulo 88); Brobbey 8 (Isidor 67, 6)

Subs (not used): Ellborg, Danso, Methalie, Fofana, Tutierov

Booked: Ahoka, Meunier, Brobbey, O'Nien, Angulo

Chelsea (4-3-3): Penders 6; Palestra 5 (Gusto 62, 5), Fofana 5, Colwill 4 (Estevao 45, 6), Chavarria 5 (Quenda 79); Caicedo 6, Lavia 6, Henderson 6 (Emegha 87); Palmer 4, Neto 5 (Welbeck 62, 5), Rogers 4

Subs (not used): Sharman-Lowe, Barco, Anselmino, Nicoll-Jazuli

Neto looked like a lost little boy trying to lead Chelsea's line in the absence of Joao Pedro.

The half-time statistics said Chelsea had sent more open-play crosses into Sunderland's box in the opening 45 minutes than in their entire games v Fulham, Everton, Tottenham, Manchester United, Bournemouth and Brighton.

Except, they had no striker for Alonso's full backs Marco Palestra or Pep Chavarria to try to find. Just 5ft 8in Neto and the odd other box-crasher.

Trailing 1-0 at half-time here, Alonso made a singular substitution. It was to introduce Estevao for Colwill, who had been tormented by Brobbey.

Le Bris was asked in his post-match press conference if there is another player like his striker in the Premier League. He thought long and hard before answering: 'What do you think? I don't think so. His physicality, his intensity, it's impressive, that's for sure. The build-up is so important to have a target man.'

Alonso chipped in on Brobbey: 'He is not unstoppable. He is stoppable but only when you defend better than we did.' On his own attack, he added: 'We didn't produce enough to deserve to win.'

Sunderland's tactic of hoofing the ball up to Brobbey worked wonders. He scared the daylights out of Chelsea's centre backs. When Fofana first arrived at the Stadium of Light, a Chelsea fan shouted at him as he got off the bus. 'Fofana, please be on the bench,' he said. Fofana may have been wishing he was a substitute as well whenever he was wrestling with Brobbey.

It was the long-ball approach which led to Sunderland winning their penalty. They smashed it towards the top of the pitch and Brobbey bullied Colwill. Sunderland won their spot-kick and, in truth, deserved the lead for the sheer energy they brought to this match.

Alonso is ten Premier League games into his Chelsea career. The honeymoon period is over. Sunderland lost their captain Granit Xhaka to an injury after two minutes here. Chelsea had named a line-up featuring three midfielders. But they never showed any signs of control, and for that, Alonso should be looking at himself and his own side rather than the refereeing team.

#1508. Real Madrid injury news: Jose Mourinho handed Aurelien Tchouameni fitness scare as France release statement

By Ben Sully | 11 Nov 2026 00:16, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 01:52

Real Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni has withdrawn from Zinedine Zidane's France squad due to injury.

France are preparing to conclude the first phase of the Nations League with an away game against Italy on Thursday and a home meeting with Turkey on Sunday.

Zidane's side are currently sitting top of the standings after collecting 10 points from their opening four games, although they still have work to do to secure a quarter-final spot.

If they are to seal a last eight berth, France will have to do it without the services of Real Madrid's Tchouameni, who has been forced to pull out of the squad with a muscular injury.

In a statement released on Tuesday evening, the French Football Federation said: “Aurelien Tchouameni is once again experiencing discomfort in his right adductor, as he did last summer during the World Cup.

"He has been dealing with this discomfort since arriving at the French National Football Centre in Clairefontaine.

"After taking his medical history into account and holding a conversation just minutes ago with Real Madrid’s medical staff, the French national team’s medical department, in agreement with the player, has decided to release him to his club.

"He will spend tonight with the squad before returning to Madrid tomorrow.”

The FFF also confirmed that no replacement will be called up, leaving Zidane with Eduardo Camavinga, Warren Zaire-Emery, Adrien Rabiot and Lucas Da Cunha as his central midfield options.

Tchouameni, who also missed the last international window, will have to wait until at least March to make his first appearance under Zidane.

Meanwhile, his latest setback will concern Real Madrid, especially as it appears to be a similar issue to the one that forced him to miss the start of the season.

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho will certainly hope the issue is a minor one, having relied heavily on Tchouameni over the last couple of months.

Los Blancos will return to action against Celta Vigo on November 11 before they face PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League just a few days later.

#1507. Key adjustments and becoming possession-oriented: Tactical analysis of Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan climbed back into the top four in the Serie A table with a much-needed win away against Genoa before the international break.

Milan found themselves two goals up inside 20 minutes when Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot and Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos, with both goals coming from the high press.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, it wouldn’t be the Rossoneri without some late drama, and Ellertsson made it a very nervy finish for the Rossoneri with a goal inside the final few minutes from a long-range strike. Milan did manage to hang on for what was an important three points.

Como’s defeat to Inter means that Ruben Amorim’s men move into the Champions League places, though after the break the pursuit of consistency will continue. Below is the tactical breakdown, from Rohit Rajeev.

Amorim chose to make five changes from Thursday’s defeat to Ferencvaros. Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all came into the side, though there were some question marks about whether it would be a four or three-man defence based on the names selected.

Genoa’s direct approach immediately put Milan on the back foot, with the hosts threatening to exploit the space behind the defensive line in the opening minute.

They played a long ball into the space behind Koni De Winter, allowing Osmanjic to run in behind and chase the delivery. Although the move appeared to be offside, it served as an early warning of the threat Genoa’s direct approach could pose to Milan’s defence.

Genoa anticipated Milan’s tendency to create numerical overloads in the wide areas and adjusted their defensive structure accordingly.

They used the corresponding centre-back, wing-back and both players from the double pivot to create a 4v3 numerical superiority against Milan’s wide combinations.

This allowed Genoa to outnumber Milan’s attacking players, restrict their progression down the flanks and make it difficult for Amorim’s side to exploit their usual wide overloads.

Milan’s in-possession structure alternated between a 4-1-4-1 and a 3-1-4-2, with the positioning of Musah largely determining which shape the team adopted.

Rabiot occupied the left half-space, while Pulisic preferred to operate closer to Moreira on the right. Meanwhile, Cisse provided the width on the left flank, functioning as Milan’s left winger.

Milan operated with a vertically staggered double pivot, comprising Modric and Rabiot. Modric occupied the deeper position, acting as the midfield screen in front of the back four and providing a link between defence and midfield.

Rabiot, meanwhile, operated higher up the pitch, effectively taking on the role of an attacking midfielder and providing an additional presence between Genoa’s midfield and defensive lines.

The move leading to Cisse’s goal began with Vasquez being tasked with progressing possession from the back. However, Milan managed to create a 3v4 numerical disadvantage for Genoa in the wide areas, forcing Vasquez to recycle possession rather than progress the ball.

Pulisic recognised the opportunity to press and initiated a ball-oriented press, eventually dispossessing Vasquez. He immediately released Rabiot, allowing Milan to exploit the turnover before Genoa could reorganise defensively.

As the possession changed hands, Ramos scanned his surroundings and identified Cisse’s position, recognising the opportunity to attack the space inside the penalty area.

Milan subsequently created a 3v2 numerical advantage inside the box. Cisse initially ran alongside Ramos before checking his run to deceive Marcandalli. This subtle change of movement created separation from his marker and allowed him to attack the space.

Rabiot delivered the cross into the penalty area, where Cisse was perfectly positioned to finish the move and give Milan the lead.

Although Milan adopted a high, man-oriented pressing structure, there were gaps that Genoa could exploit during their build-up. Musah, conscious of the possibility of Genoa creating a 2v1 situation, chose to stay closer to Diawara rather than move out to engage the ball carrier.

This left Ezhibue free to receive possession in the sizeable gap between Musah and Cisse, exposing a weakness in Milan’s pressing structure.

The move leading to Milan’s second goal began with Cisse pressing Traore from behind as the Genoa defender approached the goal line.

Under pressure, Traore attempted a cross-field pass, but Ramos positioned himself intelligently to block the passing lane towards Vasquez.

Rather than attempting to finish the move himself, Ramos showed excellent composure and unselfishly squared the ball into Pulisic’s path, despite Moreira also calling for the pass.

What made the assist particularly impressive was the Portuguese’s execution: he played a no-look pass, deceiving both the goalkeeper and the recovering defender about his intended target. Pulisic capitalised on the opportunity and converted the chance to double Milan’s advantage.

With each passing game Milan are moving into a pure possession-oriented team. In this sequence you can see Pulisic and Rabiot exchanging their positions to confuse their markers

With a 2-0 advantage, Milan shifted towards a more conservative approach, prioritising defensive stability over attacking progression. Amorim reorganised the side into a 5-4-1 defensive structure, adding greater protection to the backline and reducing the spaces available for Genoa to exploit.

However, one of the inherent vulnerabilities of a five-man defensive structure is the space left behind the wing-backs when they are drawn towards the ball.

Genoa looked to exploit this weakness by deliberately dragging Moreira out of his defensive position. As Moreira stepped forward to engage the ball carrier, Gila was forced to jump out of the defensive line to prevent Genoa from creating a 2v1 situation.

This movement consequently opened up space in the right channel, allowing Genoa to exploit an area that would otherwise have been protected by Milan’s compact 5-4-1 defensive block.

Genoa switched from their initial 3-4-2-1 to a 4-4-2 formation as they looked to change their attacking approach. El Shaarawy moved into the left midfield position, Vitinha operated on the right, while Baldanzi took up the role of a second striker.

The substitution of Marcandalli also prompted a structural change at the back, with Genoa abandoning their back three in favour of a back four. Ekhator moved into the right-back position, allowing Genoa to maintain a more conventional defensive structure.

For Genoa’s goal, Milan failed to close down Ellertsson, with the defenders seemingly anticipating a cross rather than a shot. Ellertsson recognised the opportunity and noticed that Maignan’s line of sight was obstructed by four Milan defenders.

Taking advantage of the goalkeeper’s limited visibility, he opted to shoot rather than deliver a cross, finding the back of the net.

#1506. Liverpool news: Virgil van Dijk "not in any panic" as Reds captain issues update on contract situation

By Ben Sully | 11 Nov 2026 00:56, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 01:05

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk insists he is "not in any panic" over his contract situation at Anfield.

The Netherlands international has been one of Liverpool's star players since he arrived from Southampton in the summer of 2018.

Van Dijk has made 389 appearances for the Reds, helping the club win multiple pieces of silverware, including two Premier League titles and a Champions League crown.

While he may not be at the age of 35, Van Dijk continues to play a prominent role for the Merseyside club, having started 14 of the club's 16 competitive matches this season.

As it stands, it is unclear if this is the final season of his successful Liverpool career, with his current deal set to expire at the end of the campaign.

Van Dijk has now issued an update on his contract situation, explaining that he is not stressing about his uncertain Anfield future.

“I want to keep playing and continue what I’m doing, so let’s see what the season brings,” Van Dijk told reporters.

“I’ve had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that’s the case.

"If not, then I will go somewhere else. There’s nothing to report at the moment but that doesn’t mean that there’s any stress or anything.

“I feel good but it’s not about me at the moment. I’m not in any panic whatsoever.”

With Van Dijk set to turn 36 next summer, there will be an obvious temptation to look to the long-term future and sign a younger defender who could fill Van Dijk's boots for years to come.

However, the Dutchman is still continuing to perform at a high level and has formed a strong central defensive partnership with Jeremy Jacquet this term.

The defender also plays a crucial role as captain, and his leadership will certainly be tough to replace when the time comes for him to leave Anfield.

With that in mind, the Reds should do their utmost to keep Van Dijk for at least another season, although it remains to be seen whether the player himself will look to sign a new deal or take the decision to leave while he is still performing at a high level.

In the short term, Van Dijk's current focus will be on returning to full fitness after withdrawing from Xavi's Netherlands squad with a minor issue.

By Ben Sully | 11 Nov 2026 01:35, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 01:48

Manchester United have reportedly considered new coaching support as a potential option should they decide against sacking Michael Carrick.

The Man United boss appears to be on the brink of the sack after overseeing one win in 10 Premier League games this season (D5, L4).

While his side staged a late fightback to salvage a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, the Red Devils are in a precarious position in the Premier League drop zone, with one point separating them from safety.

Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada will hold a crucial meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday.

Instead of sacking their current head coach, Man United's decision-makers could look to add coaching staff to Carrick's backroom team.

#1504. GdS: ‘Ahead of the curve’ – Amorim’s positive start compared to predecessors

Ruben Amorim might not have unanimously won everyone over yet, but AC Milan are off to their best Serie A start in four years.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write this morning that Milan under Amorim have started better than under Massimiliano Allegri in 2025-26, Paulo Fonseca in 2024-25 and even Stefano Pioli’s final season in 2023-24.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The best start belongs to the coach who delivered the Scudetto though, with 31 points in the first eleven rounds of the 2021-22 season, which ended with the most recent Italian league title added to the trophy cabinet.

Amorim has also hit the ground running, with an average that, in previous seasons, would have placed him even higher. A year ago, with 24 points at this same stage of the tournament, Milan would have been the league leaders.

The numbers don’t lie: 24 out of a possible 33 points – garnered through seven wins, three draws, and only one Serie A defeat – amount to 2.18 points per match. By comparison, Allegri had reached 22 points, Fonseca 17 and Pioli also had 22 in his final year.

The coach behind the 2021-22 Scudetto also started with great momentum in the previous season (26 points in 2022-23) and in the 2020-21 campaign (27 points).

These figures were double the 13 points from the 2019–20 season, a campaign that began with Marco Giampaolo at the helm, only for him to be replaced mid-season by Pioli. While still seeking to find that same rhythm in Europe, Milan have been surging in the league.

They got off to a blistering start with wins away at Torino and in their San Siro debut against Venezia, followed by a draw at Juventus – a match in which they were pegged back just minutes from the end -and another stalemate away to Lazio.

After falling two goals behind, Milan fought back against the team currently leading the league. Given Lazio’s subsequent form, that result takes on added significance. Next came a victory over Lecce, followed by a lacklustre draw in Reggio Emilia against Sassuolo.

From that point on, the turning point arrived: four wins in the next five matches, including away victories against Udinese and Genoa away from home, as well as the derby. The only stumble during this stretch was against Bologna.

Sensing that the squad was under significant stress, Amorim has granted a week off, with training set to resume next Monday. For those without other commitments such as international duty, this provides a chance to truly switch off.

Many players have headed away, while those who remained are either following strict injury recovery programs or simply taking a break. This pause is longer than usual: the typical break in professional leagues is generally shorter.

This isn’t the only unusual aspect: the return to training ahead of the match against Frosinone the following week will also take place only after the players returning from international duty have been given ample time to rest.

There are precedents for this, though. For instance, the team was given a Tuesday off just two days before their European away match against Bournemouth. They returned to the pitch on Wednesday, the same day they departed for England. The result was a 3-0 loss and a dark night.

There is certainly enough evidence now to speak of new methods introduced by Amorim and his staff. On the pitch, Rúben has brought in new ideas: training sessions are never overly gruelling, and the data from GPS trackers and distance-monitoring tools is never pushed to ‘excessive’ levels.

“We train by playing,” the Portuguese coach has often explained, implying that matches themselves offer the best opportunities to test tactical schemes and movements. This is especially the case when playing every three days, with such little time between games.

While this approach may have initially raised some eyebrows among the players and was even speculated to be a cause for the cluster of injuries the Rossoneri experienced, such concerns were dispelled once the coach provided further clarification.

In the meantime, no one is taking a break fully. Even while away, every player has been assigned specific training programs to follow, ensuring they return in peak condition to keep the good league form going.

#1503. New Zealand vs India - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 02:09, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 05:00

India are set for a tough test on Thursday, when they travel to Auckland's Go Media Stadium for an international friendly against New Zealand, marking their first-ever visit to the country.

The All Whites are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while the Blue Tigers are looking to follow the winning example set by their alternative squad at the SAFF Championship.

Darren Bazeley's New Zealand followed up their group-stage elimination from World Cup 2026 with a three-game unbeaten run, drawing 2-2 with Palestine before triumphing 3-0 against China and on penalties against Panama during the last international break.

However, the All Whites' streak came to an end on October 5, when they were downed 2-1 by Japan in the final of the friendly Kirin Cup.

Captain Chris Wood - the nation's record scorer and appearance holder - assisted Ben Old's equaliser that day, but he was unable to respond when Ritsu Doan netted the winner for the Samurai Blue four minutes after his second-half substitution.

Looking ahead to Thursday, the hosts have never lost to India, most recently running out 2-1 winners in the friendly AIFF Intercontinental Cup in June 2018.

However, this week's clash will be just the second time they have faced the visitors this century, and only the third meeting between the sides throughout history, after first locking horns during a goalless draw in the 1981 edition of the Merdeka Tournament.

New Zealand (ranked 88th) are the favourites to come out on top due to their 50-superior placement in FIFA's ranking system, though fans may still be cautious considering that Bazeley's team have lost two of their last three matches on home turf.

Meanwhile, Khalid Jamil's India arrive as underdogs but are keen to test their mettle in a pair of fixtures against an opponent who qualified for the World Cup.

Thursday's friendly in Auckland and Sunday's follow up in Christchurch come as part of a celebration marking 100 years of sporting connection between the nations, and the Blue Tigers' manager called for fans to join them on matchday in his press conference.

“I know there are many Indian fans here in New Zealand - I would request them to come to the stadium and support the team. Their support is important for us, and we will try to give our best on the pitch,” said Jamil.

Another challenge facing the visitors is the fact they are split across two squads, one that is set to take part in these friendlies and another that is currently contesting the 2026 SAFF Championship, the latter of which beat Pakistan 3-2 on November 5.

Beyond that victory by their alternative side, India are heading into this clash on the back of a seven-game winless run in friendlies, including a 6-1 thrashing by Uruguay and a 4-0 hammering by Brazil last month.

New Zealand International Friendlies form:

New Zealand are without right-back Callan Elliot through injury, but the versatile Bill Tuiloma could feature in his absence, joining Nando Pijnaker, Tyler Bindon and James McGarry in defence.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Chris Wood looks set to lead the line, supported from out wide by Dundee United's Jesse Randall and 20-year-old Nathan Walker of Wellington Phoenix, who could make his All Whites debut.

As for India, they have left experienced goalkeeper Gurpreet Singh Sandhu out of the squad, while centre-back Anwar Ali is sidelined due to a hamstring injury.

With that in mind, Vishal Kaith is likely to start between the sticks on Thursday, shielded by a pairing of Bijoy Varghese and Mehtab Singh.

The Blue Tigers are also without midfielder Lalengmawia Ralte, who is known as Apuia, though Anirudh Thapa could be joined by Lalrinliana Hnamte in the visitors' double pivot.

Paulsen; Tuiloma, Pijnaker, Bindon, McGarry; Rufer; Randall, Garbett, Bayliss, Walker; Wood

New Zealand are the overwhelming favourites despite featuring a number of young players in their squad, and they will be hoping to deliver a strong showing on home soil.

India will arrive knowing that they are likely to be on the losing side, but that underdog status could inspire them to find the back of the net at least once on Thursday.

#1502. Cesc Fabregas's Como win NINE-ONE in the biggest away victory in Champions League history - two weeks after thrashing Michael Carrick's Man United - in just their first year at Europe's top table

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER

Published: 17:01 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 17:59 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United's 4-1 battering by Como two weeks ago now looks a lucky escape – after the Italian side romped to a 9-1 victory at Lens in the Champions League.

Cesc Fabregas' side put in a stunning performance in a record-equalling win which well and truly announced them as contenders on the biggest stage.

Como now sit fourth in the Champions League standings after also thrashing RB Leipzig and Man United, who are likely relieved that Lens took such a pounding.

It means only Paris Saint-Germain, Real Madrid, and Arsenal have got off to better starts, despite this being their maiden season in European competition.

The lakeside outfit were 3-0 up at half-time – with the scorer of the third goal, Nico Paz, paying his respects to late Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel – before a rout after the break.

It is the latest statement win for Como, whose transformation began in 2019 when a pair of Indonesian billionaire brothers, who originally made their fortune in the tobacco industry, bought the club for $850,000 (£644,427) through their Djarum Group.

Como thrashed Lens 9-1 in a record-equalling victory in the Champions League on Wednesday

Cesc Fabregas is quickly building his name as one of the most talented coaches in Europe

With a combined net worth then estimated at $48billion (£36.4billion), Robert Budi Hartono and Michael Bambang Hartono instantly made Como the richest club in Italian football.

Rather than pursue instant success through lavish spending, Como have built steadily, investing in infrastructure, recruitment, and a clear footballing identity – and it is paying off big-time.

They have now won six games on the bounce, though they still sit fourth in Serie A five points behind leaders Lazio, who have had an almost perfect start.

Their crushing of Lens was the first time an Italian side had scored seven or more goals away from home in European Cup/Champions League history.

And their hat-trick hero on the night, Anastasios Douvikas, is now the top scorer in the Champions League ahead of Erling Haaland.

All of this comes for a side who were playing in the third tier just six seasons ago and on the back of a relatively modest summer spend of £58million on nine permanent arrivals and loanees.

'Today everything went our way,' said an ecstatic Fabregas post-match. 'A great night for Como and our fans.'

There was a poignant moment when Paz paid homage to Miguel and his hometown club, holding aloft a shirt with the picture of the late star alongside the caption: 'Rest in peace.' Though he plays for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also spent time in the club's youth system from 2014-16.

Miguel died on Tuesday morning less than 24 hours after a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during their Spanish second division match on Monday. Having suffered serious head and chest injuries he subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest.

Como's Nico Paz paid tribute to Jesus de Miguel during his goalscoring celebration vs Lens

Despite playing for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also played for their youth teams

Tenerife striker De Miguel died on Tuesday morning after a horrifying clash with Jesus Owono

Como led 3-0 at half-time with hat-trick hero Douvikas scoring two at that point before Paz's goal and his De Miguel tribute.

Soon after the interval the Serie A outfit crushed any notion of the hosts coming back as they plundered in five goals in a devastating 22-minute spell which included Douvikas completing his hat-trick. Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martina Baturina also got in on the act during that period.

Ruben Aguilar pulled one back for Lens before Matteo Papaccioli rounded off the rout in stoppage time. The 18-year-old Papaccioli, who came on in the second half, is a member of Como's youth team and hasn't even played in Serie A yet.

Wednesday's win means Como have broken many records in the Champions League.

The Italian side matched the eight-goal winning margins recorded by Liverpool and Real Madrid in their 8-0 home victories over Besiktas and Malmo respectively. They also became only the second team after Bayern Munich to score nine goals in a Champions League match.

Como followed their 4-1 victory over Manchester United with another emphatic performance, becoming the first team to score nine goals away from home in the European Cup since 1971 – Feyenoord beat Olympiacos Nicosia by this scoreline – as they climbed to fourth in the standings on nine points. The previous best scoring performance by an away club in the Champions League was Bayern Munich's 8-2 win over Barcelona at a neutral venue (Lisbon) in 2020.

Fabregas's side may have made Champions League record-equalling history, but Feyenoord hold the European Cup mark for most goals scored in a single match, having beaten Icelandic side KR 12-2 in September 1969.

Lens, who suffered the heaviest defeat by a French club in the competition, are 33rd with three points.

#1501. Guatemala vs Canada - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 11 Nov 2026 02:46

Making their first appearance in the quarter-finals of the CONCACAF Nations League, Guatemala will host Canada in the opening leg of that tie on Friday at Estadio El Trebol in Guatemala City.

A 1-0 win over Suriname helped the Guatemalans top Group B with seven points, while Canada are one of the top four ranked teams in CONCACAF, earning a bye into the knockout stage as a result.

It was a roller coaster of a group stage for Guatemala, but fortunately for them it ended with the Central Americans at the top.

Luis Fernando Tena’s men opened that phase by conceding an injury-time goal in a defeat to Jamaica (3-2) but ended it with an stoppage-time winner versus Suriname.

That victory vaulted them into the Nations League knockout stage for the first time, scoring nine goals along the way, the joint-most for them ever in the League A group phase.

Unfortunately though it came at a cost as the coach will be missing some players for this match due to the post-match altercations in that outing.

Since their heartbreaking defeat on matchday one to the Jamaicans, Guatemala have collected a clean sheet in their last three Nations League affairs, having conceded a combined 14 goals this year before this tournament began.

In their six previous League A encounters at home, this team have yet to lose, while conceding a mere two goals overall during that stretch.

Los Chapines can stretch their unbeaten run against Canada to three matches across all competitions, eliminating them on penalties in the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup quarter-finals.

Following their historic run to the last 16 of the World Cup last summer, the Canadians had a solid fall international window.

Jesse Marsch’s men won two of their three friendlies in that window, collecting two clean sheets along the way.

On Friday, they will hope to avoid consecutive international defeats for the first time since the 2024 Copa America, after losing their last international outing to the USA (1-0).

The Canucks boast a 100% away record in the quarter-finals of this tournament, winning at Jamaica in 2023 (2-1) and blanking Suriname on the road a year later (1-0).

They have won their last four internationals when netting the opening goal and have never lost a knockout match in this competition as the visiting team.

Friday will be their second Nations League match on Central American soil, with Les Rouges losing the previous one in the group stage at Honduras in 2022 (2-1).

Because of a post-match confrontation against Suriname, Jonathan Franco and Carlos Estrada will be suspended for three matches, while Oscar Santis is out due to a hamstring strain.

Matt Evans netted in the 96th minute to earn them a place in the knockout stage of this competition, his first goal on the international stage, and Nicholas Hagen collected two clean sheets in the group phase.

Canadian captain Alphonso Davies is reportedly ready to play according to Marsch, though Jonathan Osorio and Jacob Shaffelburg withdrew with injuries, while Cyle Larin was not selected because of back irritation.

Davies can move into a tie for ninth in all-time international goals Friday, while Richie Laryea will draw even with Paul Stalteri for sixth in all-time caps with his next one.

Hagen; Herrera, Yanes, Samayoa, Morales; Lopez, Castellanos, Rosales, Escobar, Rubin, Lom

Crepeau; Laryea, De Fougeroles, Ivanisevic, Davies; Buchanan, Saliba, Choiniere, Millar; J. David, Oluwaseyi

Even with Davies back, the environment in Guatemala will be difficult for the visitors to navigate, and we expect the Central Americans’ suffocating defence to limit the scoring chances for Canada.

#1500. Moretto: Milan’s plan for rising star Cisse clear as Brighton see approach rejected

Alphadjo Cisse is attracting interest after his red-hot start to the season, and AC Milan are already rejecting advances.

Cisse is undoubtedly the story of the season for Milan so far. Having officially signed from Hellas Verona in January, he was allowed to remain on loan with Catanzaro in Serie B before suffering a serious injury that needed surgery. After a few months out, a loan was even evaluated.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yet, Ruben Amorim saw something in the 20-year-old and made him a big part of his plans. His faith has been rewarded, given that Cisse has eight goals in 12 appearances in all competitions so far this season, with the latest coming against Genoa on Sunday.

These numbers have naturally attracted the interest of several European clubs, but there is also talk of a renewal. Matteo Moretto explained things in a video on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“Milan are rejecting verbal offers from several clubs. Milan are already saying no to several clubs for Cisse. There are several Premier League clubs, and I’ll name one, Brighton,” the journalist began.

“Milan have already said no and wants to renew his contract. And they will renew his contract, which currently expires in 2030. There will be a salary adjustment. Born in 2006, nine games and five goals [in Serie A]. Incredible talent, just called up by Mancini.

“I also want to give credit to the old Rossoneri management, because whoever signed him – the Furlani-Moncada duo – snatched him from PSV, who had practically sealed the deal. When the player saw Milan appear, he had no doubts and turned down PSV.

“Even the sporting project, sending him on loan to Catanzaro, was key for the player. Because the path was the right one, and today we can see the results. Milan paid €8m, having tried to sign him in previous years from Verona Primavera. Congratulations to Milan and to all the management linked to Cisse.”

#1499. Guimaraes looks a £75m bargain as ‘super sub’ makes difference

Arsenal have played six Premier League games this season and Bruno Guimarães has been a match-winning force in two of them. At this rate, he might justify his enormous £75m transfer fee by Christmas.

The Brazilian was not signed to be Arsenal’s super sub but that is the role he appears to be playing in these early days in north London. Against Leeds United here, as it was against Sunderland last month, he came off the bench when the champions were struggling. And as it was at Sunderland, he produced a thumping finish to put Arsenal on their way to three points.

Liquid football from Arsenal 😮‍💨 Bruno Guimarães finishes off a well-worked team move! 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/fbLJiaZbX5

This is the value of signing a 28-year-old with significant Premier League experience. As Arsenal laboured against an impressively organised and courageous Leeds side, Mikel Arteta knew that Guimarães was capable of coming into the game and adjusting to its demands. There has been no adaptation period required for Guimarães, who is fast becoming one of the most popular players in north London.

The finish, which put Arsenal 2-1 ahead at the Emirates Stadium, marked an emphatic conclusion to a fabulous passing sequence. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice all combined at speed before Guimarães charged on to Rice’s flick. “It was a beauty,” said Arteta of the goal. The move had actually begun at the feet of Guimarães a few moments earlier, when he nutmegged an opponent in style.

The winning goal came just eight minutes after Riccardo Calafiori, Arsenal’s thrilling left-back/centre-forward hybrid, had pulled them level in the game. James Justin had struck for Leeds shortly after half-time, creating a horrible anxiety among the home fans here, and for much of the afternoon Daniel Farke’s side were the better team.

Leeds finally have their opener! 🤩 James Justin arrives at the back post to fire them ahead. 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/ITjUMSlrG1

Leeds, though, could not compete with Arsenal for depth. The arrival of Guimarães as a 63rd-minute substitute represented a flexing of Arteta’s managerial muscle, in his first match since signing a new long-term contract, and the Brazilian offered a moment of attacking quality that his opponents were unable to replicate.

It was actually the first competitive home game that Guimarães had played for Arsenal since his transfer from Newcastle United, as a result of a few niggles and the club’s unusual run of four consecutive away matches before the international break. The most recent of those was the 3-0 thrashing by Brighton, which was one of their worst defeats of the last few seasons.

This gritty victory represented a necessary response to that defeat, even if the performance was far from dominant. “We had a point to prove,” said Arteta. “Something was touched in our identity against Brighton.”

Guimarães, too, clearly felt that some wrongs needed to be made right. For all his brilliance in this game and against Sunderland, he had produced a horrible showing at the Amex Stadium a few weeks ago. “He was not at that level against Brighton,” said Arteta. “This is the level for Arsenal. Every week, every game, every minute, every action you have to be at that level. At Brighton, he wasn’t. Today, he was much better.”

Leeds had not lost in their opening five Premier League matches of this season and it was easy to see why. They were willing to press Arsenal high up the pitch, taking risks and engaging in physical duels, and the strategy proved hugely effective for an hour.

If they had been more precise in the final third, they could have been a few goals ahead by the time Justin converted Gabriel Gudmundsson’s left-wing cross after 55 minutes. Anton Stach, who was accidentally blocked by team-mate Jayden Bogle, and Gudmundsson both went close in the first half.

The early kick-off, the long international break, the slow start and the memories of the Brighton defeat made it a strange atmosphere at the Emirates. You would not have known they were the champions, based on the reaction of the fans to the first-half performance, but the achievements of last season clearly do not guarantee fervent support at all times.

Calafiori’s equaliser, which marked his fifth goal involvement in 10 games for club and country this season, changed the momentum of the game. Yunus Musah has been one of the surprises of the season for AC Milan. Now, the management have begun talks over his contract.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

“I congratulate you because you’ve had two difficult years. I know you’re a guy who’s suffered a lot, but you’ve never given up,” the former full-back said.

“I can assure you of this because I’ve watched you work together for years. It’s truly been a great pleasure, so congratulations, and don’t get too big for your boots, but I’m sure you won’t because you’re a good guy.”

These were sincere words from someone who has experienced the Milan dressing room and knows how difficult it can be to succeed.

One of the key figures behind Musah’s new-found form is Ruben Amorim. The Portuguese coach completely revitalised him after two very difficult seasons, relying on him from day one and receiving a lot of hard work and dedication in return.

Amorim’s vision demands a player with Musah’s characteristics: a powerful engine, a remarkable ability to transform a passive game into an active one, and excellent transition skills. Versatility helps too, given that against Genoa the manager even deployed him as a left-back.

Musah’s season so far has seen him make 11 league appearances, with a total of 759 minutes played, plus three in the Europa League, with 222 minutes played. Going into preseason, that kind of reliance seemed impossible.

It’s not just Amorim who’s satisfied with Musah’s performances but the entire management as well, so much so that in recent days they’ve even discussed the possibility of extending his contract, which expires in 2028.

Recent contacts with the player’s entourage have helped them begin evaluating the possibility of renewing his deal. Musah currently earns around €2m per season and – if he maintains this level – he will sign new terms before the end of the season.

#1497. Woltemade involved in both goals but VAR denies Lucumí as Juventus draw 2-2 with Rennes

Nick Woltemade created Juventus's opener and scored their equaliser, but Jhon Lucumí's late winner against Rennes was ruled out for offside. The draw in Turin moves Spalletti's side to seven points in the Europa League league phase ahead of Sunday's trip to Lecce.

Juventus came within a VAR decision of beating Rennes at the Allianz Stadium on Thursday 22 October. Jhon Lucumí found the net in the 90th minute. Referee Morten Krogh studied the pitchside monitor and disallowed the goal for offside. Eight minutes of stoppage time followed, and the match finished 2-2.

Nick Woltemade was central to both Juventus goals. Spalletti’s side now sit on seven points after three league-phase matches. They had lost 0-3 to Lazio in their previous game.

Zeki Çelik put Juventus ahead in the fifth minute from Woltemade’s pass. Mousa Al-Tamari equalised in the 15th minute, set up by Bryan Reynolds. Federico Gatti was booked in the 19th minute for stopping the Rennes goalkeeper from taking a quick clearance.

Weston McKennie hit the post at around the half-hour mark with the score still level. Rennes then won a penalty when Douglas Luiz was penalised for handball. Boulaye Dia converted it in the 43rd minute, and the visitors led 1-2 at the break. Çelik, the scorer of the opener, went off injured after 45 minutes. Al-Tamari earned the match’s top rating from the data provider, 8.2.

The equaliser came from the spot. Reynolds blocked a Nico González header with his arm away from his body, and VAR upheld the award. Woltemade scored the penalty in the 67th minute. He finished with seven shots and two key passes.

Juventus generated expected goals of 2.25 against 1.72 for Rennes. They also had 54% of possession. Rennes took more shots, 16 to 14, and put more on target, five to four. Juventus were caught offside three times, while the visitors were never flagged. Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal was booked in the 82nd minute for time wasting.

Both sides were short of key players. Spalletti was without the injured Locatelli, Yildiz, Thuram, Grabara, Ekhator and Conceição. Zhegrova and Milik were unavailable because they are not on the UEFA squad list. Antonio Stefano Merola was in the 21-man squad after his first senior call-up. Rennes were missing their leading scorer Lepaul, who was injured and did not travel from France.

FT |⌛️| Finisce in parità all’Allianz Stadium#JuveSRFC #UEL pic.twitter.com/QaF2LuUDp9

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) October 22, 2026

Krogh had refereed nine Europa League matches and one Champions League match before this game. He had never taken charge of either club.

Juventus’s next Europa League fixtures are away to AZ Alkmaar on 5 November 2026 and at home to Omonia on 26 November 2026. Before that, Serie A resumes. Lecce host Juventus on matchday 8, with Eusebio Di Francesco’s side kicking off against Spalletti’s at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday 25 October.

#1496. GdS: The full story of Milan and Inter’s record-breaking €650m deal with Generali

More details continue to emerge regarding the stadium naming rights deal between AC Milan, Inter and Generali.

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that even before it’s even been built, the new home of Milan and Inter is already the place to be. It’s no coincidence that Generali – the insurance giant – has decided to put its stamp on the façades, as was revealed last month at the presentation of the stadium.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The collaboration kicks off immediately. Generali are now the Official Insurance Partner of the two clubs. The stadium naming rights contract will last for 25 years and includes the payment of €50m until the stadium opens in 2031.

This includes €10m annually for each of the next five seasons, including the current one, to be split equally between Inter and Milan. Once the stadium is inaugurated, the sum will increase to €30m annually (€15m each) for the following 20 years. The total commitment amounts to €650m.

Generali wanted to associate its name with the stadium from the very beginning of this long journey, in order to establish itself in the collective imagination: it will only be the Generali Stadium, with no temporary or secondary names to muddy the waters.

Branding a stadium from day one – or rather, even before it opens – is particularly strategic in terms of marketing. For this reason, Generali have agreed to pay €10m a year for something that, for five years, will be on models and then on construction sites, but not yet in the experience of fans.

Moreover, the naming rights market still has ample room for development in Europe. A Kroll study of the 36 major European clubs highlighted this already in 2024: only 12 had sold the naming rights to their stadiums, for a total estimated potential value of €303m, equivalent to an average of €8.4m per season.

Italy and England were the leagues least inclined to this form of commercialisation, also held back by the historical connection between the stadiums and their names. In this scenario, the new Inter and Milan stadium represents a different opportunity: a stadium to be built around a commercial identity,.

It’s not just a sports sponsorship: it’s a key support for a project crucial to the next stage of development of the city, the beating heart of the country’s economy and finances. This explains the significant investment.

It was the first time Inter and Milan worked together on the same side of the table, to secure a commercial deal. Under the watchful eye of Oaktree and RedBird Capital, the two clubs’ Chief Revenue Officers – Giorgio Ricci and Maikel Oettle – took the lead in finalising the sale of the naming rights.

These will be transferred through Stadio San Siro, a company controlled by NSM Holding, equally owned by Milan and Inter. The Rossoneri and Nerazzurri had initially selected a small group of potential partners, focusing on major Italian companies.

This type of right is particularly attractive to companies with a strong interest in the local area. After an initial round of meetings, Generali was the company that immediately showed the most enthusiasm.

Inter and AC Milan thus decided to further discuss the deal with the insurance giant, finalising the contract within a few months, the largest ever signed by Generali in the sports sector. In addition to the price offered, a key factor was the partner’s status.

Who better than the insurance giant – with €4.3bn in net profit and €900bn in assets under management – can offer guarantees of solidity and solvency, especially in a long-term commitment?

The €650m is written in stone and represents a significant portion of the financial coverage for the entire real estate transaction. Moreover, thanks to the €50m ‘bridge’ payment, the clubs have the opportunity to cash in immediately.

A comparison with other major international stadiums further illustrates the scale of the operation. Once fully operational, with €30m annually, the Generali Stadium will rank at the top of the global naming rights market, becoming one of the most lucrative deals ever signed for a stadium.

In Europe, the benchmark is Spotify’s Camp Nou, which guarantees Barcelona €20m per season, while Bayern Munich earn around €13m annually from Allianz for the Munich Arena. London’s Emirates Stadium is currently worth an estimated €10-15m to Arsenal.

Atletico Madrid’s Riyadh Air Metropolitano is at a similar level to that of the Gunners. In Germany, Borussia Dortmund get around €11m for Signal Iduna Park. Juventus, with the Allianz Stadium, earns around €8-10m.

To find higher figures, one must look primarily to the United States, where the stadium sponsorship market is of a different size and characteristics. The Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles is worth approximately €31m annually, but the $700m twenty-year contract also includes other commercial activities of the AEG group and partnerships with the Lakers and Kings.

The same is true for SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, whose twenty-year, $625m agreement equates to approximately €28m annually, but includes additional commercial components. Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, on the other hand, has signed a thirty-year agreement worth approximately $750m, equivalent to approximately €22m per season.

These transactions should be interpreted with caution, as the consideration does not always refer solely to the naming of the stadium. The Milan figure, however, is significant precisely because of the size of the naming rights component.

There is also another aspect to consider. The €30m guaranteed by Generali could represent only the first step in a much broader commercial strategy. An ecosystem of partnerships will develop around the new stadium, from technology services to beverage supplies, and other product categories that can be accommodated in the facility.

The goal is to raise an additional €20-25 million through agreements with secondary sponsors, bringing the overall value of the stadium’s commercial partnerships to even higher levels. Meanwhile, the market is also starting to move in Italy, albeit on a much smaller scale.

Atalanta earn approximately €2.5m annually from its partnership with New Balance for the naming of the New Balance Arena, while Udinese earns approximately €1m Bluenergy for the Bluenergy Stadium.

In short, the Milan deal risks rewriting the industry benchmarks, pushing up the valuations of other European venues and confirming how the name of a stadium, when associated with an international project, is a valuable asset.could become a top-level commercial asset.

#1494. Celik and Nico Gonzalez injuries add to Juventus absences before Lecce

Juventus will travel to Lecce without Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez after both players picked up muscle injuries in Thursday’s 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes, adding two more names to an already long absence list for Luciano Spalletti.

The club confirmed the diagnoses in an official medical update on Friday, October 23. Both players had felt muscle discomfort after the Rennes match and went for tests at J|medical that morning.

According to the club, Celik has a low-grade injury to the biceps femoris in his left leg, while Nico Gonzalez has a low-grade injury to the soleus muscle in his right calf. Juventus said both players have already started their rehabilitation programmes, but the statement did not give a return date for either of them.

Medical Update | Çelik and Nico González’s conditions

🗞️ https://t.co/BHwNzeidQ7 pic.twitter.com/YUXRK97IwL

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 23, 2026

The timing is frustrating for Celik in particular. The Turkish full-back opened the scoring against Rennes in the fifth minute, converting a pass from Nick Woltemade, before being taken off at half-time. You can read how the rest of that night unfolded in our report on the Rennes draw.

Juventus have not put a timeframe on either recovery, so any estimate comes from the Italian press. Virgilio Sport reports that both players are expected to be out for around 20 days and should only return after the November international break, with the home game against Venezia on November 22 named as the first realistic target.

If that estimate holds, the pair would miss the trip to Lecce, the meeting with Genoa, the home game against Napoli, the Europa League visit to AZ Alkmaar and the match with Fiorentina. That is a demanding run to face with a thinner squad, and it comes at a point when Juventus are trying to recover from the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio.

Celik and Nico Gonzalez join Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Francisco Conceicao on the sidelines, according to Tuttosport. Conceicao is already in rehabilitation after the shoulder problem he picked up against Lazio, as covered in our Francisco Conceicao injury update.

Tuttosport’s expected line-up has Spalletti sticking with a 3-5-2, with Pierre Kalulu and Andrea Cambiaso on the flanks and Woltemade partnering Randal Kolo Muani in attack. The match at the Via del Mare kicks off at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday, October 25, with Maresca as referee.

Supporters will also have to wait until matchday to hear from the coach. Tuttosport reports that Spalletti, in agreement with the club, will not hold his usual press conference on the eve of the Lecce game. The paper links the decision to the packed schedule after the Europa League fixture, and Virgilio Sport notes that Spalletti has taken the same approach before during congested spells, with no controversy behind the choice.

The squeeze on the squad is now the bigger story. With two more first-team players ruled out and the injury list still growing, Spalletti will need his remaining options to carry the load through a busy stretch of Serie A and European fixtures before the international break.

Sources: Juventus FC, Tuttosport, Virgilio Sport

#1493. Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”

Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.
